findings_addressed.oracle: Exact equality to Python-language-semantic oracle values: print('hello') produces 'hello\n' and print(1) produces '1\n'. These are independently derived from CPython's str() + newline concatenation, not from any value injected by the test. The assertion is now result['output'] == expected_output (exact equality), not a truthy check.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation:

'). This produces 'PREFIXhello

findings_addressed.oracle: Positive equality assertion: doc.search_text_calls[0]['encoding'] == 'latin1'. The encoding provider is configured to return 'latin1', so the only correct behaviour is to forward exactly 'latin1'. The previous negative assertion (!= 'utf-8') would still pass if _resolve_search_encoding always returned 'ascii' or any other non-utf8 string.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/ui/panels/hex_editor/scripting.py, change _resolve_search_encoding to always return 'ascii' (ignoring the encoding_provider). The new equality assertion '== latin1' fails because 'ascii' != 'latin1'. The old '!= utf-8' assertion would still pass.

notes:
Wave-2 re-hardening: (1) test_print_output_captured now uses exact equality (result['output'] == expected_output) with per-parametrize-case oracle values derived from Python semantics rather than a bare truthy .strip() check; the parametrize tuple was extended to carry the expected string.
